import type { Metadata, Viewport } from "next";
import { Inter } from "next/font/google";
import "./globals.css";
import { SiteHeader } from "@/components/site-header";
import { SiteFooter } from "@/components/site-footer";

const inter = Inter({ subsets:["latin"], variable:"--font-inter", display:"swap" });

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: { default: "MapleRoute — Your guide to Canadian permanent residence", template: "%s · MapleRoute" },
  description: "A guided companion for Canada's Express Entry process, with a CRS points checker. Independent and not affiliated with IRCC.",
};
export const viewport: Viewport = { themeColor: "#ffffff" };

export default function RootLayout({children}) {
 return (
  <html lang="en" className={inter.variable}>
   <body className="flex min-h-dvh flex-col bg-canvas font-sans text-ink antialiased">
     <a href="#main" className="...">Skip to content</a>
     <SiteHeader />
     <main id="main" className="flex-1">{children}</main>
     <SiteFooter />
   </body>
  </html>
 );
}

{
  "content": "\"use client\";\n\nimport { useEffect, useRef, useState, type ReactNode } from \"react\";\n\ntype RevealProps = {\n  children: ReactNode;\n  delay?: number;\n  className?: string;\n};\n\nexport function Reveal({ children, delay = 0, className = \"\" }: RevealProps) {\n  const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);\n  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const node = ref.current;\n    if (!node) return;\n\n    if (window.matchMedia(\"(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)\").matches) {\n      setVisible(true);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const observer = new IntersectionObserver(\n      (entries) => {\n        if (entries[0]?.isIntersecting) {\n          setVisible(true);\n          observer.disconnect();\n        }\n      },\n      { threshold: 0.15, rootMargin: \"0px 0px -8% 0px\" },\n    );\n\n    observer.observe(node);\n    return () => observer.disconnect();\n  }, []);\n\n  return (\n    <div\n      ref={ref}\n      className={`reveal ${visible ? \"is-visible\" : \"\"} ${className}`}\n      style={{ transitionDelay: `${delay}ms` }}\n    >\n      {children}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n",
  "file_path": "C:\\Users\\Admin\\MapleRoute\\components\\reveal.tsx"
}

```js
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  content: ["./src/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}"],
  presets: [require("nativewind/preset")],
  theme: { extend: {} },
  plugins: [],
}

module.exports = function (api) {

      "nativewind/babel",
    ],
  };
};
```

const { getDefaultConfig } = require("expo/metro-config");

Root layout:
```tsx
import "react-native-gesture-handler"; // gesture handler import first? For Expo Router not strictly needed.
import { useFonts, Inter_400Regular, ... } from "@expo-google-fonts/inter";
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import * as SplashScreen from "expo-splash-screen";
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { SafeAreaProvider } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
import { StatusBar } from "expo-status-bar";
import * as SystemUI from "expo-system-ui";
import { Platform } from "react-native";
import "../global.css";

SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync();

export default function RootLayout() {
  const [fontsLoaded, fontError] = useFonts({...});
  useEffect(() => {
    if (Platform.OS !== "web") {
      SystemUI.setBackgroundColorAsync(tokens.colors.canvas).catch(() => {});
    }
  }, []);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (fontsLoaded || fontError) SplashScreen.hideAsync();
  }, [fontsLoaded, fontError]);
  if (!fontsLoaded && !fontError) return null;
  return (
    <SafeAreaProvider>
      <StatusBar style="dark" backgroundColor={...} />
      <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false, contentStyle: { backgroundColor: canvas } }}>
        <Stack.Screen name="(tabs)" />
      </Stack>
    </SafeAreaProvider>
  );
}
```
Import path: global.css is at src/global.css; layout at src/app/_layout.tsx → "../global.css".

`SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync()` at module top returns promise; add `.catch(() => {})` to avoid unhandled.

Fonts: Inter_400Regular, Inter_500Medium, Inter_600SemiBold, Inter_700Bold from @expo-google-fonts/inter. Note font family names in useFonts keys: the package exports names identical. Pass { Inter_400Regular, ... }.

Hook implementation:
```ts
type HealthSnapshot = { status: "checking"|"connected"|"error"|"unconfigured"; latencyMs?: number; checkedAt?: Date; error?: string; host?: string };
export function useSupabaseHealth() {
 const [snapshot, setSnapshot] = useState<HealthSnapshot>({status: "checking"});
 const mounted = useRef(true);
 const check = useCallback(async () => {
   setSnapshot({status:"checking"});
   if (!isSupabaseConfigured) { setSnapshot({status:"unconfigured"}); return; }
   const controller = new AbortController();
   const timeout = setTimeout(()=>controller.abort(), 10000);
   const started = performance.now? Date.now();
   try {
     const res = await fetch(`${supabaseUrl}/auth/v1/health`, {headers:{apikey:anonyKey, Authorization:`Bearer ${anonKey}`}, signal: controller.signal});
     ...
   } catch (e) { setSnapshot({status:"error", error: message}); }
   finally { clearTimeout(timeout); }
 }, []);
 useEffect(() => { check(); }, [check]);
 return { snapshot, check };
}
```
Need mounted guard to avoid state update after unmount; keep AbortController; check function shouldn't set after unmount. Use a ref. Since Home remains mounted across tabs (tabs keep screens), not a big issue. Still implement.

Let's design a proper maple leaf with 11 points but broader, with deeper notches and wider body. Key: maple leaf has 3 main lobes at top (top point + two upper side points) plus 2 lower lobes each side, and a stem. The current has points all around evenly like a star.

- Central top point.
- On each side, a small upper notch and an upper point.
- Then an inward notch and a big side point.
- Then inward notch and lower side point.
- Then the bottom lobes beside the stem.
- Stem at bottom.

import { Text as RNText, type TextProps as RNTextProps } from "react-native";
export type TextVariant = "display" | "title" | "heading" | "body" | "small" | "label" | "button";
export type TextTone = "ink" | "muted" | "accent" | "white";
const variantClasses: Record<TextVariant, string> = {
  display: "text-[34px] leading-[40px] font-inter-semibold tracking-[-0.9px]",
  title: "text-[26px] leading-[32px] font-inter-semibold tracking-[-0.5px]",
  heading: "text-[18px] leading-[25px] font-inter-semibold tracking-[-0.2px]",
  body: "text-[15px] leading-[23px] font-inter",
  small: "text-[13px] leading-[19px] font-inter",
  label: "text-[11px] leading-[15px] font-inter-semibold uppercase tracking-[1.4px]",
  button: "text-[15px] leading-[20px] font-inter-semibold",
};
const toneClasses = { ink:"text-ink", muted:"text-muted", accent:"text-accent", white:"text-white" };
type Props = RNTextProps & { variant?: TextVariant; tone?: TextTone; className?: string };
export function Text({ variant="body", tone="ink", className="", ...rest }: Props) {
  return <RNText className={`${variantClasses[variant]} ${toneClasses[tone]} ${className}`} {...rest} />;
}
```
RN Text doesn't have className typing without nativewind types; nativewind-env adds it globally. Good.

import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { Animated, Easing, Platform, type ViewStyle } from "react-native";
export function FadeIn({ children, delay=0, distance=10, className }: ...) {
 const progress = useRef(new Animated.Value(0)).current;
 useEffect(() => {
   const anim = Animated.timing(progress, { toValue:1, duration:450, delay, easing:Easing.out(Easing.cubic), useNativeDriver: Platform.OS !== "web" });
   anim.start();
   return () => anim.stop();
 }, [delay, progress]);
 const translateY = progress.interpolate({ inputRange:[0,1], outputRange:[distance,0] });
 return <Animated.View style={{ opacity: progress, transform:[{translateY}] }} className={className}>{children}</Animated.View>;
}
```

export type ConnectionStatus = "checking" | "connected" | "unconfigured" | "error";
export type ConnectionSnapshot = { status; latencyMs?: number; checkedAt?: Date; error?: string; };
export function useSupabaseHealth() {
 const [snapshot, setSnapshot] = useState<ConnectionSnapshot>({ status: "checking" });
 const requestRef = useRef(0);
 const check = useCallback(async () => {
   const id = ++requestRef.current;
   if (!isSupabaseConfigured) { setSnapshot({status:"unconfigured"}); return; }
   setSnapshot({status:"checking"});
   const started = Date.now();
   const controller = new AbortController();
   const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 10000);
   try {
     const res = await fetch(`${supabaseUrl}/auth/v1/health`, {
       headers: { apikey: supabaseAnonKey, Authorization: `Bearer ${supabaseAnonKey}` },
       signal: controller.signal,
     });
     if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Supabase replied with HTTP ${res.status}.`);
     await res.json().catch(() => undefined);
     if (requestRef.current === id) setSnapshot({ status: "connected", latencyMs: Date.now()-started, checkedAt: new Date() });
   } catch (error) {
     if (requestRef.current !== id) return;
     let message = "We couldn't reach Supabase. Check the project URL and your connection.";
     if (error instanceof Error) {
       if (error.name === "AbortError") message = "The request timed out after 10 seconds.";
       else if (error.message.startsWith("Supabase replied")) message = error.message;
     }
     setSnapshot({ status: "error", error: message });
   } finally { clearTimeout(timeout); }
 }, []);
 useEffect(() => { void check(); return () => { requestRef.current++; }; }, [check]);
 return { snapshot, check };
}
```
Timeout race causes AbortError; friendly.

`src/lib/supabase.ts`:
```ts
import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";

const url = (process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL ?? "").trim().replace(/\/+$/, "");
const anonKey = (process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY ?? "").trim();

export const supabaseUrl = url;
export const supabaseAnonKey = anonKey;
export const isSupabaseConfigured = /^https?:\/\//.test(url) && anonKey.length > 0;

// Session persistence moves to expo-secure-store when auth is added.
export const supabase = isSupabaseConfigured
  ? createClient(url, anonKey, {
      auth: { persistSession: false, autoRefreshToken: false, detectSessionInUrl: false },
    })
  : null;

export function getSupabaseHost(): string | null {
  if (!isSupabaseConfigured) return null;
  try { return new URL(url).host; } catch { return url.replace(/^https?:\/\//, ""); }
}
```
Should we prevent invalid URL from being considered configured? isSupabaseConfigured checks http(s). Error state would be "setup needed" for malformed URL, hiding the actual issue. Better treat any non-empty url+key as configured so the check runs and surfaces a URL error. Use `url.length > 0 && anonKey.length > 0`; createClient with "localhost" might throw at creation? createClient validates URL? It might throw "Invalid supabaseUrl" if empty only. A malformed URL could cause constructor error. Keep regex validation but show a specific setup state? For phase 0, simpler: configured = both non-empty. Create client inside try/catch? Since health uses fetch directly, client not needed for UI. If createClient throws at module load, app crashes. Supabase-js createClient throws when supabaseUrl missing; with malformed string it may accept and fail later. To be safe:
```ts
function createSupabaseClient() { if (!url || !anonKey) return null; try { return createClient(...) } catch { return null; } }
export const isSupabaseConfigured = Boolean(url && anonKey);
```
This avoids crash. Fine.

{
  "content": "import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from \"react\";\n\nimport {\n  isSupabaseConfigured,\n  supabaseAnonKey,\n  supabaseUrl,\n} from \"@/lib/supabase\";\n\nexport type ConnectionStatus = \"checking\" | \"connected\" | \"unconfigured\" | \"error\";\n\nexport type ConnectionSnapshot = {\n  status: ConnectionStatus;\n  latencyMs?: number;\n  checkedAt?: Date;\n  error?: string;\n};\n\nexport function useSupabaseHealth() {\n  const [snapshot, setSnapshot] = useState<ConnectionSnapshot>({\n    status: \"checking\",\n  });\n  const requestId = useRef(0);\n\n  const check = useCallback(async () => {\n    const id = ++requestId.current;\n\n    if (!isSupabaseConfigured) {\n      setSnapshot({ status: \"unconfigured\" });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    setSnapshot({ status: \"checking\" });\n\n    const startedAt = Date.now();\n    const controller = new AbortController();\n    const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 10_000);\n\n    try {\n      const response = await fetch(`${supabaseUrl}/auth/v1/health`, {\n        headers: {\n          apikey: supabaseAnonKey,\n          Authorization: `Bearer ${supabaseAnonKey}`,\n        },\n        signal: controller.signal,\n      });\n\n      if (!response.ok) {\n        throw new Error(`Supabase replied with HTTP ${response.status}.`);\n      }\n\n      await response.json().catch(() => undefined);\n\n      if (requestId.current !== id) return;\n\n      setSnapshot({\n        status: \"connected\",\n        latencyMs: Date.now() - startedAt,\n        checkedAt: new Date(),\n      });\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (requestId.current !== id) return;\n\n      let message =\n        \"We couldn't reach Supabase. Check the project URL and your connection.\";\n      if (error instanceof Error) {\n        if (error.name === \"AbortError\") {\n          message = \"The connection timed out after 10 seconds.\";\n        } else if (error.message.startsWith(\"Supabase replied\")) {\n          message = error.message;\n        }\n      }\n\n      setSnapshot({ status: \"error\", error: message });\n    } finally {\n      clearTimeout(timeout);\n    }\n  }, []);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    void check();\n    return () => {\n      requestId.current += 1;\n    };\n  }, [check]);\n\n  return { snapshot, check };\n}\n",

}

import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { ActivityIndicator, Pressable, type PressableProps } from "react-native";
import { hapticLight } from "@/lib/haptics";
import { colors } from "@/theme/theme";
import { Text } from "./text";

type ButtonProps = Omit<PressableProps, "children"> & {
 label: string;
 loading?: boolean;
 loadingLabel?: string;
 icon?: ReactNode;
};

export function Button({label, loading=false, loadingLabel="Please wait…", icon, disabled, onPress, className="", ...rest}: ButtonProps) {
 const inactive = disabled || loading;
 return (
  <Pressable
    accessibilityRole="button"
    accessibilityState={{ disabled: inactive, busy: loading }}
    disabled={inactive}
    onPress={(event) => {
      hapticLight();
      onPress?.(event);
    }}
    className={`h-[52px] flex-row items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-control bg-accent px-5 active:bg-accent-pressed ${inactive ? "opacity-60" : ""} ${className}`}
    {...rest}
  >
   {loading ? <ActivityIndicator size="small" color={colors.canvas}/> : icon}
   <Text variant="button" tone="white">{loading ? loadingLabel : label}</Text>
  </Pressable>
 );
}

\"alert-circle-outline\" : \"key-outline\"}\n        size={21}\n        color={status === \"error\" ? colors.accent : colors.ink}\n      />\n    </View>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction SetupSteps() {\n  const steps = [\n    \"Copy .env.example to .env at the project root.\",\n    \"Add your project URL and anon key.\",\n    \"Restart Expo, then check again.\",\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <View className=\"mt-5 rounded-control bg-surface p-4\">\n      <Text variant=\"label\" tone=\"muted\">\n        To connect\n      </Text>\n\n      <View className=\"mt-3 gap-3\">\n        {steps.map((step, index) => (\n          <View key={step} className=\"flex-row items-start gap-3\">\n            <View className=\"mt-0.5 h-5 w-5 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-canvas\">\n              <Text variant=\"code\" tone=\"muted\">\n                {index + 1}\n              </Text>\n            </View>\n            <Text variant=\"small\" tone=\"muted\" className=\"flex-1\">\n              {step}\n            </Text>\n          </View>\n        ))}\n      </View>\n\n      <View className=\"mt-4 gap-1 rounded-[10px] border border-line bg-canvas p-3\">\n        <Text variant=\"code\">EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL</Text>\n        <Text variant=\"code\">EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY</Text>\n      </View>\n\n      <Text variant=\"small\" tone=\"muted\" className=\"mt-3\">\n        Use the anon key only — never the service_role key.\n      </Text>\n    </View>\n  );\n}\n\nexport function ConnectionCard({\n  snapshot,\n  onRetry,\n}: {\n  snapshot: ConnectionSnapshot;\n  onRetry: () => void;\n}) {\n  const title =\n    snapshot.status === \"error\"\n      ? \"Not connected\"\n      : statusCopy[snapshot.status].title;\n  const description =\n    snapshot.status === \"error\"\n      ? (snapshot.error ??\n        \"We couldn't reach Supabase. Check your project and try again.\")\n      : statusCopy[snapshot.status].description;\n\n  const showDetails = snapshot.status === \"connected\";\n\n  return (\n    <Card className=\"p-5\">\n      <View className=\"flex-row items-start gap-3.5\">\n        <StatusBadge status={snapshot.status} />\n        <View className=\"flex-1 pt-0.5\">\n          <Text variant=\"label\" tone=\"muted\">\n            Supabase\n          </Text>\n          <Text variant=\"title\" className=\"mt-1\">\n            {title}\n          </Text>\n          <Text variant=\"small\" tone=\"muted\" className=\"mt-1.5\">\n            {description}\n          </Text>\n        </View>\n      </View>\n\n      {showDetails && (\n        <View className=\"mt-5 rounded-control bg-surface px-4\">\n          <DetailRow label=\"Project\" value={getSupabaseHost() ?? \"—\"} />\n          <Divider />\n          <DetailRow\n            label=\"Response\"\n            value={`${Math.max(1, snapshot.latencyMs ?? 0)} ms`}\n          />\n          <Divider />\n          <DetailRow label=\"Checked\" value={formatTime(snapshot.checkedAt)} />\n        </View>\n      )}\n\n      {snapshot.status === \"error\" && (\n        <View className=\"mt-4 rounded-control bg-surface p-3\">\n          <Text variant=\"small\" tone=\"muted\">\n            Check that the project is active and the URL points to your project\n            — not the database or pooler host.\n          </Text>\n        </View>\n      )}\n\n      {snapshot.status === \"unconfigured\" && <SetupSteps />}\n\n      <Button\n        className=\"mt-5\"\n        label={showDetails ? \"Check again\" : \"Check connection\"}\n        loadingLabel=\"Checking…\"\n        loading={snapshot.status === \"checking\"}\n        onPress={onRetry}\n        icon={\n          <Ionicons name=\"refresh\" size={16} color={colors.canvas} />\n        }\n      />\n    </Card>\n  );\n}\n",

const fs = require("fs");

const ws = new WebSocket(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl);
await new Promise(res=>ws.onopen=res);
let id=0; const pending=new Map();
ws.onmessage = ev => { const msg=JSON.parse(ev.data); if(msg.id&&pending.has(msg.id)){pending.get(msg.id)(msg);pending.delete(msg.id);} };
const send=(method,params={})=>new Promise((resolve,reject)=>{const i=++id;pending.set(i,(m)=>m.error?reject(new Error(JSON.stringify(m.error))):resolve(m.result));ws.send(JSON.stringify({id:i,method,params}));});
await send("Page.enable");
await send("Runtime.enable");

await send("Page.navigate",{url:"http://localhost:8081/"});
await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,6000));
const metrics = await send("Runtime.evaluate",{expression:`JSON.stringify({innerWidth:window.innerWidth,scrollWidth:document.documentElement.scrollWidth, ...})`,returnByValue:true});

const shot = await send("Page.captureScreenshot",{format:"png",captureBeyondViewport:false});
fs.writeFileSync(".qoder-home-mobile.png", Buffer.from(shot.data,"base64"));
...

arg.description ?? \"\")\n        .join(\" \"),\n    );\n  }\n};\n\nfunction send(method, params = {}) {\n  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n    const id = ++messageId;\n    pending.set(id, { resolve, reject });\n    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }));\n  });\n}\n\nawait send(\"Page.enable\");\nawait send(\"Runtime.enable\");\n\nasync function capture({ url, width, height, mobile, file, fullPage = false }) {\n  await send(\"Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride\", {\n    width,\n    height,\n    deviceScaleFactor: 2,\n    mobile,\n    screenWidth: width,\n    screenHeight: height,\n  });\n  await send(\"Page.navigate\", { url });\n  await sleep(6500);\n\n  const metrics = await send(\"Runtime.evaluate\", {\n    expression: `(() => {\n      const root = document.getElementById(\"root\");\n      return JSON.stringify({\n        innerWidth: window.innerWidth,\n        innerHeight: window.innerHeight,\n        docScrollWidth: document.documentElement.scrollWidth,\n        docScrollHeight: document.documentElement.scrollHeight,\n        bodyScrollWidth: document.body.scrollWidth,\n        rootWidth: root ?   "content": "# MapleRoute\n\nMapleRoute is a step-by-step companion for applying for Canadian Permanent Residence. It is an independent guide — not legal or immigration advice, and not affiliated with IRCC or the Government of Canada.\n\nThe app is built with Expo (React Native + TypeScript) so one codebase runs on iOS, Android, and the web.\n\n**Current status: Phase 0 — foundation.** The app shell, design tokens, brand assets, and a live Supabase connection check are in place. There are no database tables, accounts, or immigration content yet.\n\n## What Phase 0 includes\n\n- Native tab navigation (Home, Settings) with the MapleRoute design system.\n- A Home screen that checks the Supabase project from the device and shows one of four states: `Setup needed`, `Connecting…`, `Connected`, or `Not connected`.\n- A Settings screen with version, Supabase host, the independent-guide notice, and the privacy boundary (MapleRoute never asks for an IRCC password, UCI, or passport number).\n- App icons, splash image, favicon, EAS build profiles, and `.env.example`.\n\nThe connection check calls Supabase's public health endpoint (`/auth/v1/health`), so it works before any tables are created.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- Node.js 20 or newer (this project was verified on Node 24).\n- npm (included with Node).\n- For a physical phone: the free **Expo Go** app from the App Store or Google Play.\n- Optional, for native builds: an Expo account and `eas-cli`. Xcode (macOS) or Android Studio is only needed if you want to compile locally.\n\n## 1. Install\n\n```bash\nnpm install\n```\n\n## 2. Connect Supabase\n\n1. Create a project at https://supabase.com (or open the existing one).\n2. In the Supabase dashboard, open **Project Settings → API**.\n3. Copy the **Project URL** and the **anon public** key.\n4. Create your local env file:\n\n   macOS / Linux / Git Bash / PowerShell:\n\n   ```bash\n   cp .env.example .env\n   ```\n\n   Windows Command Prompt:\n\n   ```bat\n   copy .env.example .env\n   ```\n\n5. Edit `.env` and fill in both values:\n\n   ```\n   EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project-ref.supabase.co\n   EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-public-key\n   ```\n\n6. Restart the dev server. Expo inlines `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values when the bundle starts, so changes do not apply to an already-running server.\n\nUse **only** the anon public key in this app. Never put the `service_role` key in `.env` or anywhere in the client — it bypasses Row Level Security. Everything prefixed with `EXPO_PUBLIC_` is visible to anyone who inspects the app.\n\n## 3. Run it\n\n### Website (local)\n\n```bash\nnpm run web\n```\n\nOpen http://localhost:8081. The layout is centred at a readable width on desktop and fills the screen on mobile.\n\n### Phone with Expo Go\n\n1. Put the phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi network.\n2. Start the dev server:\n\n   ```bash\n   npm run start:go\n   ```\n\n3. Scan the QR code: Camera app on iOS, or the Expo Go app's scanner on Android.\n\nIf your network blocks device-to-computer connections, use a tunnel:\n\n```bash\nnpx expo start --go --tunnel\n```\n\n`npm start` (without `--go`) opens the development build if one is installed. Use `npm run start:go` when you specifically want Expo Go.\n\n### Native development build (optional, later)\n\nA development build is a real app binary that can use custom native modules. It is not required for Phase 0.\n\n```bash\nnpx eas-cli@latest login\nnpx eas-cli@latest init\nnpx eas-cli@latest build --profile development --platform android\n# or: --platform ios  (iOS device builds require an Apple Developer account)\n```\n\nInstall the resulting build on the device, then run:\n\n```bash\nnpx expo start --dev-client\n```\n\nThe EAS profiles in `eas.json`:\n\n| Profile | Use it for | Distribution |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `development` | Day-to-day development with a dev client | Internal |\n| `preview` | Test builds for testers | Internal |\n| `production` | App Store / Play Store releases | Store |\n\n```bash\nnpx eas-cli@latest build --profile preview --platform all\nnpx eas-cli@latest build --profile production --platform all\n```\n\n## Scripts\n\n| Command | What it does |\n| --- | --- |\n| `npm start` | Start the Expo dev server (dev client if installed) |\n| `npm run start:go` | Start Expo and force Expo Go |\n| `npm run web` | Start the web version in a browser |\n| `npm run android` / `npm run ios` | Open on an emulator/simulator |\n| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript check with no output files |\n| `npm run lint` | Expo's ESLint setup |\n\n## Project structure\n\n```\nsrc/\n  app/\n    _layout.tsx          Root layout: fonts, splash, status bar, safe areas\n    (tabs)/\n      _layout.tsx        Bottom tab bar\n      index.tsx          Home: connection check and what's next\n      settings.tsx       App details, disclaimer, privacy boundary\n  components/\n    brand.tsx            Maple leaf mark and brand lockup\n    connection-card.tsx  Supabase status card and setup steps\n    disclaimer.tsx       Independent-guide notice\n    screen.tsx           Shared page frame (safe area, scroll, width)\n    ui/                  Text, Button, Card, DetailRow, Divider\n  hooks/\n    use-supabase-health.ts\n  lib/\n    supabase.ts          Client + configuration check\n    haptics.ts           Native haptics, no-op on web\n  theme/\n    tokens.json          Single source of truth for colour, radius, spacing\n    theme.ts             Typed token exports\n    shadow.ts            Cross-platform card shadow\nassets/images/           App icon, Android adaptive icon, splash, favicon\n```\n\nDesign tokens live in `src/theme/tokens.json` and are consumed by both `tailwind.config.js` and TypeScript. Change a colour there once and both the styles and native styles pick it up.\n\n## Web build and hosting\n\nCreate a static build:\n\n```bash\nnpx expo export --platform web\n```\n\nThe output goes to `dist/`. Expo's web output is a single-page app, so a static host must rewrite unknown paths to `index.html`. On Netlify that is a `netlify.toml` at the project root:\n\n```toml\n[[redirects]]\n  from = \"/*\"\n  to = \"/index.html\"\n  status = 200\n```\n\nHosting, the privacy policy, and the support page will be handled in a later phase.\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n- **The Home card still says \"Setup needed\"**: `.env` is missing, both values are not filled in, or the dev server was started before you saved `.env`. Stop the server, confirm the file is at the project root, and start it again.\n- **\"Not connected\" with a timeout**: the device cannot reach the Supabase URL. Check the URL, your internet connection, and that the Supabase project is not paused.\n- **Port 8081 is busy**: another Expo/Metro process is still running. Close it, or start with `npx expo start --web --port 8082`.\n- **Expo Go shows an incompatible SDK message**: update Expo Go from the app store — this project uses Expo SDK 58.\n\n## Data and privacy boundaries\n\nPhase 0 stores nothing. Authentication, cloud sync, and account deletion arrive in a later phase and will be built on Supabase Auth, Postgres with Row Level Security, and `expo-secure-store`. MapleRoute will never ask for an IRCC password, UCI, or passport number unless a specific feature is approved and explained first.\n\nImmigration requirements, fees, and steps will be stored as data with a `source_url` (canada.ca / IRCC), a `last_verified` date, and a version — not hardcoded in screens.\n"
}
```

  "content": "import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from \"react\";\n\nimport {\n  isSupabaseConfigured,\n  supabaseAnonKey,\n  supabaseUrl,\n} from \"@/lib/supabase\";\n\nexport type ConnectionStatus = \"checking\" | \"connected\" | \"unconfigured\" | \"error\";\n\nexport type ConnectionSnapshot = {\n  status: ConnectionStatus;\n  latencyMs?: number;\n  checkedAt?: Date;\n  error?: string;\n};\n\nexport function useSupabaseHealth() {\n  const [snapshot, setSnapshot] = useState<ConnectionSnapshot>({\n    status: \"checking\",\n  });\n  const requestId = useRef(0);\n\n  const check = useCallback(async () => {\n    const id = ++requestId.current;\n\n    if (!isSupabaseConfigured) {\n      setSnapshot({ status: \"unconfigured\" });\n      return;\n    }\n\n    setSnapshot({ status: \"checking\" });\n\n    const startedAt = Date.now();\n    const controller = new AbortController();\n    const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 10_000);\n\n    try {\n      const response = await fetch(`${supabaseUrl}/auth/v1/health`, {\n        headers: {\n          apikey: supabaseAnonKey,\n          Authorization: `Bearer ${supabaseAnonKey}`,\n        },\n        signal: controller.signal,\n      });\n\n      if (!response.ok) {\n        throw new Error(`Supabase replied with HTTP ${response.status}.`);\n      }\n\n      await response.json().catch(() => undefined);\n\n      if (requestId.current !== id) return;\n\n      setSnapshot({\n        status: \"connected\",\n        latencyMs: Date.now() - startedAt,\n        checkedAt: new Date(),\n      });\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (requestId.current !== id) return;\n\n      let message =\n        \"We couldn't reach Supabase. Check the project URL and your connection.\";\n      if (error instanceof Error) {\n        if (error.name === \"AbortError\") {\n          message = \"The connection timed out after 10 seconds.\";\n        } else if (error.message.startsWith(\"Supabase replied\")) {\n          message = error.message;\n        }\n      }\n\n      setSnapshot({ status: \"error\", error: message });\n    } finally {\n      clearTimeout(timeout);\n    }\n  }, []);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    void check();\n    return () => {\n      requestId.current += 1;\n    };\n  }, [check]);\n\n  return { snapshot, check };\n}\n",

}

  "content": "# MapleRoute\n\nMapleRoute is a step-by-step companion for applying for Canadian Permanent Residence. It is an independent guide — not legal or immigration advice, and not affiliated with IRCC or the Government of Canada.\n\nThe app is built with Expo (React Native + TypeScript) so one codebase runs on iOS, Android, and the web.\n\n**Current status: Phase 0 — foundation.** The app shell, design tokens, brand assets, and a live Supabase connection check are in place. There are no database tables, accounts, or immigration content yet.\n\n## What Phase 0 includes\n\n- Native tab navigation (Home, Settings) with the MapleRoute design system.\n- A Home screen that checks the Supabase project from the device and shows one of four states: `Setup needed`, `Connecting…`, `Connected`, or `Not connected`.\n- A Settings screen with version, Supabase host, the independent-guide notice, and the privacy boundary (MapleRoute never asks for an IRCC password, UCI, or passport number).\n- App icons, splash image, favicon, EAS build profiles, and `.env.example`.\n\nThe connection check calls Supabase's public health endpoint (`/auth/v1/health`), so it works before any tables are created.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- Node.js 20 or newer (this project was verified on Node 24).\n- npm (included with Node).\n- For a physical phone: the free **Expo Go** app from the App Store or Google Play.\n- Optional, for native builds: an Expo account and `eas-cli`. Xcode (macOS) or Android Studio is only needed if you want to compile locally.\n\n## 1. Install\n\n```bash\nnpm install\n```\n\n## 2. Connect Supabase\n\n1. Create a project at https://supabase.com (or open the existing one).\n2. In the Supabase dashboard, open **Project Settings → API**.\n3. Copy the **Project URL** and the **anon public** key.\n4. Create your local env file:\n\n   macOS / Linux / Git Bash / PowerShell:\n\n   ```bash\n   cp .env.example .env\n   ```\n\n   Windows Command Prompt:\n\n   ```bat\n   copy .env.example .env\n   ```\n\n5. Edit `.env` and fill in both values:\n\n   ```\n   EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project-ref.supabase.co\n   EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-public-key\n   ```\n\n6. Restart the dev server. Expo inlines `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values when the bundle starts, so changes do not apply to an already-running server.\n\nUse **only** the anon public key in this app. Never put the `service_role` key in `.env` or anywhere in the client — it bypasses Row Level Security. Everything prefixed with `EXPO_PUBLIC_` is visible to anyone who inspects the app.\n\n## 3. Run it\n\n### Website (local)\n\n```bash\nnpm run web\n```\n\nOpen http://localhost:8081. The layout is centred at a readable width on desktop and fills the screen on mobile.\n\n### Phone with Expo Go\n\n1. Put the phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi network.\n2. Start the dev server:\n\n   ```bash\n   npm run start:go\n   ```\n\n3. Scan the QR code: Camera app on iOS, or the Expo Go app's scanner on Android.\n\nIf your network blocks device-to-computer connections, use a tunnel:\n\n```bash\nnpx expo start --go --tunnel\n```\n\n`npm start` (without `--go`) opens the development build if one is installed. Use `npm run start:go` when you specifically want Expo Go.\n\n### Native development build (optional, later)\n\nA development build is a real app binary that can use custom native modules. It is not required for Phase 0.\n\n```bash\nnpx eas-cli@latest login\nnpx eas-cli@latest init\nnpx eas-cli@latest build --profile development --platform android\n# or: --platform ios  (iOS device builds require an Apple Developer account)\n```\n\nInstall the resulting build on the device, then run:\n\n```bash\nnpx expo start --dev-client\n```\n\nThe EAS profiles in `eas.json`:\n\n| Profile | Use it for | Distribution |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `development` | Day-to-day development with a dev client | Internal |\n| `preview` | Test builds for testers | Internal |\n| `production` | App Store / Play Store releases | Store |\n\n```bash\nnpx eas-cli@latest build --profile preview --platform all\nnpx eas-cli@latest build --profile production --platform all\n```\n\n## Scripts\n\n| Command | What it does |\n| --- | --- |\n| `npm start` | Start the Expo dev server (dev client if installed) |\n| `npm run start:go` | Start Expo and force Expo Go |\n| `npm run web` | Start the web version in a browser |\n| `npm run android` / `npm run ios` | Open on an emulator/simulator |\n| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript check with no output files |\n| `npm run lint` | Expo's ESLint setup |\n\n## Project structure\n\n```\nsrc/\n  app/\n    _layout.tsx          Root layout: fonts, splash, status bar, safe areas\n    (tabs)/\n      _layout.tsx        Bottom tab bar\n      index.tsx          Home: connection check and what's next\n      settings.tsx       App details, disclaimer, privacy boundary\n  components/\n    brand.tsx            Maple leaf mark and brand lockup\n    connection-card.tsx  Supabase status card and setup steps\n    disclaimer.tsx       Independent-guide notice\n    screen.tsx           Shared page frame (safe area, scroll, width)\n    ui/                  Text, Button, Card, DetailRow, Divider\n  hooks/\n    use-supabase-health.ts\n  lib/\n    supabase.ts          Client + configuration check\n    haptics.ts           Native haptics, no-op on web\n  theme/\n    tokens.json          Single source of truth for colour, radius, spacing\n    theme.ts             Typed token exports\n    shadow.ts            Cross-platform card shadow\nassets/images/           App icon, Android adaptive icon, splash, favicon\n```\n\nDesign tokens live in `src/theme/tokens.json` and are consumed by both `tailwind.config.js` and TypeScript. Change a colour there once and both the styles and native styles pick it up.\n\n## Web build and hosting\n\nCreate a static build:\n\n```bash\nnpx expo export --platform web\n```\n\nThe output goes to `dist/`. Expo's web output is a single-page app, so a static host must rewrite unknown paths to `index.html`. On Netlify that is a `netlify.toml` at the project root:\n\n```toml\n[[redirects]]\n  from = \"/*\"\n  to = \"/index.html\"\n  status = 200\n```\n\nHosting, the privacy policy, and the support page will be handled in a later phase.\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n- **The Home card still says \"Setup needed\"**: `.env` is missing, both values are not filled in, or the dev server was started before you saved `.env`. Stop the server, confirm the file is at the project root, and start it again.\n- **\"Not connected\" with a timeout**: the device cannot reach the Supabase URL. Check the URL, your internet connection, and that the Supabase project is not paused.\n- **Port 8081 is busy**: another Expo/Metro process is still running. Close it, or start with `npx expo start --web --port 8082`.\n- **Expo Go shows an incompatible SDK message**: update Expo Go from the app store — this project uses Expo SDK 58.\n\n## Data and privacy boundaries\n\nPhase 0 stores nothing. Authentication, cloud sync, and account deletion arrive in a later phase and will be built on Supabase Auth, Postgres with Row Level Security, and `expo-secure-store`. MapleRoute will never ask for an IRCC password, UCI, or passport number unless a specific feature is approved and explained first.\n\nImmigration requirements, fees, and steps will be stored as data with a `source_url` (canada.ca / IRCC), a `last_verified` date, and a version — not hardcoded in screens.\n"
}

52	 What are high-wage occupations in the Express Entry system 
53	 How we determine eligible high-wage occupations for Express Entry 
54	 Express Entry high-wage occupations list 
55	 What are high-wage occupations in the Express Entry system? 
56	 Under Express Entry, a job is considered a high-wage occupation if the median wage of all people in Canada performing that job is at least 1.3 times higher than the average median wage of the overall Canadian work force. 
57	 This is based on all the people in Canada working under the same National Occupational Classification (NOC). 
58	 It is not determined based on a person’s specific job position or salary. 
59	 High-wage occupations are grouped into 3 levels using NOC codes where the median wage is at least: 
60	 twice the average median wage
61	 1.5 times, but less than twice, the average median wage 
62	 1.3 times, but less than 1.5 times, the average median wage 
63	 How we determine eligible high-wage occupations for Express Entry
64	 We use data from these sources over the last 3 years to determine the high-wage occupation level for each job:
65	 The Job Bank 
66	 The Labour Force Survey , and 
67	 The Census of Population . 
68	 For each NOC, its high-wage occupation level is determined based on the highest level its median wage met in the last 3 years.
69	 What happens to my application if the high-wage occupation list is updated?
70	 If the high-wage occupation list changes after we issue an Invitation to Apply (ITA), we’ll keep using the level that applied on the date we invited you. 
71	 This applies if a job:
72	 moves levels on the list 
73	 is removed from the list, or 
74	 is added to the list
75	 Express Entry high-wage occupations list 
76	 Comes into effect on November 3, 2026
77	 The list is currently based on data from 2023 to 2025.

introduce points for eligible Canadian work experience or qualifying job offers in high-­wage occupations , and
 remove labour market impact assessment (LMIA) requirements for qualifying job offers used to establish program eligibility and obtain Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) points
 What candidates need to know
 Candidates who may qualify for job offer points should review and update their Express Entry profiles before November 3 to verify that all required job offer information is included and accurate.
 How the new points will work
 Candidates may qualify for points based on either
 eligible Canadian work experience based on its duration, with additional points where the experience is in a high-wage occupation, or
 a qualifying job offer in a high-wage occupation
 Candidates who qualify under both will receive whichever option provides more points. The points for Canadian work experience and a job offer will not be combined.
 The maximum number of points available under the labour market integration factor is 150 points for candidates without an accompanying spouse or common-law partner and 140 points for candidates with an accompanying spouse or common-law partner.
 Receiving additional CRS points does not guarantee an invitation to apply. Invitations will continue to depend on the requirements and CRS cut-off score for each invitation round.
 Points for Canadian work experience in a high-wage occupation
 Candidates with at least one year of eligible Canadian work experience in a high-wage occupation may receive additional CRS points based on the wage level of their occupation.
 High-wage occupation level | 
 Additional CRS points | 
 At least 12 months in one or more occupations at 2 times the median | 
 70 | 
 If not eligible for 70 points, at least 12 months combined in occupations at 1.5 times the median or above | 
 40 | 
 If not eligible for 40 or 70 points, at least 12 months combined across eligible high-wage occupations (1.3 times the median or above) | 
 20 | 
 These points are in addition to a candidate's CRS score based on the duration of their eligible Canadian work experience, up to a maximum of 80 points for 5 years. Combined, candidates with eligible Canadian work experience in a high-wage occupation could receive up to 150 points for Canadian work experience.
 Candidates with Canadian work experience that does not qualify for high-wage occupation points will continue to receive points for the duration of their eligible Canadian work experience.
 Eligible Canadian work experience generally must have been acquired in Canada within the previous 10 years in an occupation in TEER category 0, 1, 2 or 3 of the National Occupational Classification. Specific provisions also apply to certain physicians providing publicly funded medical services.
 Points for a qualifying job offer in a high-wage occupation
 Candidates with a qualifying job offer in a high-wage occupation may receive: 
 High-wage occupation level | 
 CRS points | 
 At least 2 times the median wage | 
 100 | 
 At least 1.5 times the median wage | 
 70 | 
 At least 1.3 times the median wage | 
 50 | 
 A qualifying job offer must generally be for full-time, continuous work in Canada for at least one year after the candidate becomes a permanent resident.
 Specific requirements apply to certain occupations, including skilled trades and physicians providing publicly funded medical services.
 Single assessment process for qualifying job offers
 Beginning November 3, 2026, an LMIA will not be required for a qualifying job offer to be eligible for the new Express Entry points. 
 A temporary public policy will also exempt candidates invited to apply on or after November 3, 2026, from all requirements related to LMIA and LMIA exemptions for qualifying job offers used to establish eligibility under the Federal Skilled Worker Program and Federal Skilled Trades Program , provided they meet the conditions of the public policy.
 IRCC will continue to verify qualifying job offers and take measures to identify and address potential fraud or misrepresentation. Limiting job offer points to high-wage occupations also supports verification, as many of these occupations require specialized skills, experience or qualifications that can be assessed as part of the application.
 How job offers will be assessed
 An IRCC officer must determine that a qualifying job offer is genuine, including whether
 the employer is actively engaged in the business for which the offer is being made
 the offer reflects the employer's reasonable employment needs
 the employer can reasonably meet the terms of the offer
 the candidate is qualified and able to perform the work and is likely to accept and carry out the employment
 the employer has complied with applicable federal and provincial employment and recruitment laws
 A job offer that is revoked will no longer qualify.

authErrorMessage(error: unknown) {\n  const message =\n    error instanceof Error\n      ? error.message\n      : typeof error === \"string\"\n        ? error\n        : \"Something went wrong. Try again.\";\n  const lower = message.toLowerCase();\n\n  if (lower.includes(\"invalid login credentials\")) {\n    return \"That email and password don't match. Check them and try again.\";\n  }\n  if (lower.includes(\"email not confirmed\")) {\n    return \"Confirm your email first. We sent you a link when you signed up.\";\n  }\n  if (lower.includes(\"already registered\") || lower.includes(\"already exists\")) {\n    return \"An account with this email already exists. Sign in instead.\";\n  }\n  if (lower.includes(\"password should be at least\")) {\n    return \"Use a password with at least 8 characters.\";\n  }\n  if (lower.includes(\"rate limit\") || lower.includes(\"too many\")) {\n    return \"Too many attempts. Wait a minute, then try again.\";\n  }\n  if (lower.includes(\"supabase is not configured\")) {\n    return \"Accounts aren't connected yet. Add your Supabase keys first.\";\n  }\n  if (lower.includes(\"google sign-in is available\")) {\n    return \"Google sign-in is available on the web version first.\";\n  }\n  return message;\n}\n"
}

(JSON.parse(raw) as T) : null;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nexport function writeLocalValue(key: string, value: unknown) {\n  const store = storage();\n  if (!store) return;\n  try {\n    store.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(value));\n  } catch {\n    // Storage can be full or blocked; the score still shows for this session.\n  }\n}\n\nexport function removeLocalValue(key: string) {\n  const store = storage();\n  if (!store) return;\n  try {\n    store.removeItem(key);\n  } catch {\n    // Ignore unavailable storage.\n  }\n}\n"
}

}

import fs from "node:fs";

const PORT = process.env.CDP_PORT ?? "9333";
const BASE = "http://localhost:8081";
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

async function getPageTarget() {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 40; attempt += 1) {
    try {
      const targets = await (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/list`)).json();
      const page = targets.find((target) => target.type === "page");
      if (page?.webSocketDebuggerUrl) return page;
    } catch {}
    await sleep(250);
  }
  throw new Error("No debuggable page found");
}

const target = await getPageTarget();
const ws = new WebSocket(target.webSocketDebuggerUrl);
await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
  ws.onopen = resolve;
  ws.onerror = reject;
});

let messageId = 0;
const pending = new Map();
const consoleErrors = [];

ws.onmessage = (event) => {
  const message = JSON.parse(event.data);
  if (message.id && pending.has(message.id)) {
    const { resolve, reject } = pending.get(message.id);
    pending.delete(message.id);
    if (message.error) reject(new Error(JSON.stringify(message.error)));
    else resolve(message.result);
    return;
  }
  if (message.method === "Runtime.exceptionThrown") {
    consoleErrors.push(
      message.params.exceptionDetails?.exception?.description ??
        message.params.exceptionDetails?.text ??
        "Unknown exception",
    );
  }
  if (message.method === "Runtime.consoleAPICalled" && message.params.type === "error") {
    consoleErrors.push(
      message.params.args.map((arg) => arg.value ?? arg.description ?? "").join(" "),
    );
  }
};

function send(method, params = {}) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const id = ++messageId;
    pending.set(id, { resolve, reject });
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }));
  });
}

async function evaluate(expression) {
  const result = await send("Runtime.evaluate", {
    expression,
    returnByValue: true,
    awaitPromise: true,
  });
  return result.result?.value;
}

async function setViewport(width, height, mobile) {
  await send("Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride", {
    width,
    height,
    deviceScaleFactor: 2,
    mobile,
    screenWidth: width,
    screenHeight: height,
  });
}

**Response:**

1	# MapleRoute
2	
3	MapleRoute is a step-by-step companion for applying for Canadian Permanent Residence. It is an independent guide — not legal or immigration advice, and not affiliated with IRCC or the Government of Canada.
4	
5	The app is built with Expo (React Native + TypeScript) so one codebase runs on iOS, Android, and the web.
6	
7	**Current status: Phase 0 — foundation.** The app shell, design tokens, brand assets, and a live Supabase connection check are in place. There are no database tables, accounts, or immigration content yet.
8	
9	## What Phase 0 includes
10	
11	- Native tab navigation (Home, Settings) with the MapleRoute design system.
12	- A Home screen that checks the Supabase project from the device and shows one of four states: `Setup needed`, `Connecting…`, `Connected`, or `Not connected`.
13	- A Settings screen with version, Supabase host, the independent-guide notice, and the privacy boundary (MapleRoute never asks for an IRCC password, UCI, or passport number).
14	- App icons, splash image, favicon, EAS build profiles, and `.env.example`.
15	
16	The connection check calls Supabase's public health endpoint (`/auth/v1/health`), so it works before any tables are created.
17	
18	## Prerequisites
19	
20	- Node.js 20 or newer (this project was verified on Node 24).
21	- npm (included with Node).
22	- For a physical phone: the free **Expo Go** app from the App Store or Google Play.
23	- Optional, for native builds: an Expo account and `eas-cli`. Xcode (macOS) or Android Studio is only needed if you want to compile locally.
24	
25	## 1. Install
26	
27	```bash
28	npm install
29	```
30	
31	## 2. Connect Supabase
32	
33	1. Create a project at https://supabase.com (or open the existing one).
34	2. In the Supabase dashboard, open **Project Settings → API**.
35	3. Copy the **Project URL** and the **anon public** key.
36	4. Create your local env file:
37	
38	   macOS / Linux / Git Bash / PowerShell:
39	
40	   ```bash
41	   cp .env.example .env
42	   ```
43	
44	   Windows Command Prompt:
45	
46	   ```bat
47	   copy .env.example .env
48	   ```
49	
50	5. Edit `.env` and fill in both values:
51	
52	   ```
53	   EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project-ref.supabase.co
54	   EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-public-key
55	   ```
56	
57	6. Restart the dev server. Expo inlines `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values when the bundle starts, so changes do not apply to an already-running server.
58	
59	Use **only** the anon public key in this app. Never put the `service_role` key in `.env` or anywhere in the client — it bypasses Row Level Security. Everything prefixed with `EXPO_PUBLIC_` is visible to anyone who inspects the app.
60	
61	## 3. Run it
62	
63	### Website (local)
64	
65	```bash
66	npm run web
67	```
68	
69	Open http://localhost:8081. The layout is centred at a readable width on desktop and fills the screen on mobile.
70	
71	### Phone with Expo Go
72	
73	1. Put the phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi network.
74	2. Start the dev server:
75	
76	   ```bash
77	   npm run start:go
78	   ```
79	
80	3. Scan the QR code: Camera app on iOS, or the Expo Go app's scanner on Android.
81	
82	If your network blocks device-to-computer connections, use a tunnel:
83	
84	```bash
85	npx expo start --go --tunnel
86	```
87	
88	`npm start` (without `--go`) opens the development build if one is installed. Use `npm run start:go` when you specifically want Expo Go.
89	
90	### Native development build (optional, later)
91	
92	A development build is a real app binary that can use custom native modules. It is not required for Phase 0.
93	
94	```bash
95	npx eas-cli@latest login
96	npx eas-cli@latest init
97	npx eas-cli@latest build --profile development --platform android
98	# or: --platform ios  (iOS device builds require an Apple Developer account)
99	```
100	
101	Install the resulting build on the device, then run:
102	
103	```bash
104	npx expo start --dev-client
105	```
106	
107	The EAS profiles in `eas.json`:
108	
109	| Profile | Use it for | Distribution |
110	| --- | --- | --- |
111	| `development` | Day-to-day development with a dev client | Internal |
112	| `preview` | Test builds for testers | Internal |
113	| `production` | App Store / Play Store releases | Store |
114	
115	```bash
116	npx eas-cli@latest build --profile preview --platform all
117	npx eas-cli@latest build --profile production --platform all
118	```
119	
120	## Scripts
121	
122	| Command | What it does |
123	| --- | --- |
124	| `npm start` | Start the Expo dev server (dev client if installed) |
125	| `npm run start:go` | Start Expo and force Expo Go |
126	| `npm run web` | Start the web version in a browser |
127	| `npm run android` / `npm run ios` | Open on an emulator/simulator |
128	| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript check with no output files |
129	
130	## Project structure
131	
132	```
133	src/
134	  app/
135	    _layout.tsx          Root layout: fonts, splash, status bar, safe areas
136	    (tabs)/
137	      _layout.tsx        Bottom tab bar
138	      index.tsx          Home: connection check and what's next
139	      settings.tsx       App details, disclaimer, privacy boundary
140	  components/
141	    brand.tsx            Maple leaf mark and brand lockup
142	    connection-card.tsx  Supabase status card and setup steps
143	    disclaimer.tsx       Independent-guide notice
144	    screen.tsx           Shared page frame (safe area, scroll, width)
145	    ui/                  Text, Button, Card, DetailRow, Divider
146	  hooks/
147	    use-supabase-health.ts
148	  lib/
149	    supabase.ts          Client + configuration check
150	    haptics.ts           Native haptics, no-op on web
151	  theme/
152	    tokens.json          Single source of truth for colour, radius, spacing
153	    theme.ts             Typed token exports
154	    shadow.ts            Cross-platform card shadow
155	assets/images/           App icon, Android adaptive icon, splash, favicon
156	```
157	
158	Design tokens live in `src/theme/tokens.json` and are consumed by both `tailwind.config.js` and TypeScript. Change a colour there once and both the styles and native styles pick it up.
159	
160	## Web build and hosting
161	
162	Create a static build:
163	
164	```bash
165	npx expo export --platform web
166	```
167	
168	The output goes to `dist/`. Expo's web output is a single-page app, so a static host must rewrite unknown paths to `index.html`. On Netlify that is a `netlify.toml` at the project root:
169

172	  from = "/*"
173	  to = "/index.html"
174	  status = 200
175	```

178	
179	## Troubleshooting
180	
181	- **The Home card still says "Setup needed"**: `.env` is missing, both values are not filled in, or the dev server was started before you saved `.env`. Stop the server, confirm the file is at the project root, and start it again.
182	- **"Not connected" with a timeout**: the device cannot reach the Supabase URL. Check the URL, your internet connection, and that the Supabase project is not paused.
183	- **Port 8081 is busy**: another Expo/Metro process is still running. Close it, or start with `npx expo start --web --port 8082`.
184	- **Expo Go shows an incompatible SDK message**: update Expo Go from the app store — this project uses Expo SDK 58.
185	
186	## Data and privacy boundaries
187	
188	Phase 0 stores nothing. Authentication, cloud sync, and account deletion arrive in a later phase and will be built on Supabase Auth, Postgres with Row Level Security, and `expo-secure-store`. MapleRoute will never ask for an IRCC password, UCI, or passport number unless a specific feature is approved and explained first.
189	
190	Immigration requirements, fees, and steps will be stored as data with a `source_url` (canada.ca / IRCC), a `last_verified` date, and a version — not hardcoded in screens.

-- MapleRoute Phase 1: accounts and CRS snapshots
-- Run this in Supabase Dashboard > SQL Editor > New query.

-- One profile row per authenticated user.
create table if not exists public.profiles (
  id uuid primary key references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  email text,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

alter table public.profiles enable row level security;

drop policy if exists "profiles_select_own" on public.profiles;
drop policy if exists "profiles_update_own" on public.profiles;

create policy "profiles_select_own"
  on public.profiles for select
  to authenticated
  using ((select auth.uid()) = id);

create policy "profiles_update_own"
  on public.profiles for update
  to authenticated
  using ((select auth.uid()) = id)
  with check ((select auth.uid()) = id);

-- Create the profile automatically when someone signs up.
create or replace function public.handle_new_user()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  insert into public.profiles (id, email)
  values (new.id, new.email)
  on conflict (id) do nothing;
  return new;
end;
$$;

drop trigger if exists on_auth_user_created on auth.users;
create trigger on_auth_user_created
  after insert on auth.users
  for each row execute function public.handle_new_user();

-- Every CRS check is kept so the applicant can see how their score changes.
create table if not exists public.crs_snapshots (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  score integer not null check (score between 0 and 1200),
  breakdown jsonb not null,
  inputs jsonb not null,
  rules_version text not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create index if not exists crs_snapshots_user_created_idx
  on public.crs_snapshots (user_id, created_at desc);

alter table public.crs_snapshots enable row level security;

drop policy if exists "crs_snapshots_select_own" on public.crs_snapshots;
drop policy if exists "crs_snapshots_insert_own" on public.crs_snapshots;
drop policy if exists "crs_snapshots_delete_own" on public.crs_snapshots;

create policy "crs_snapshots_select_own"
  on public.crs_snapshots for select
  to authenticated
  using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);

create policy "crs_snapshots_insert_own"
  on public.crs_snapshots for insert
  to authenticated
  with check ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);

create policy "crs_snapshots_delete_own"
  on public.crs_snapshots for delete
  to authenticated
  using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);

#### Thinking

Important finding: production build navigating directly to `/settings` redirects to `/login` because preview mode is React state lost on full page reload. But in production, a signed-in user session persists via Supabase, so /settings would load. In preview (no Supabase), preview mode doesn't persist across reloads — acceptable but slightly annoying. Could persist preview mode flag in localStorage so reloads keep preview. That would make preview more usable and testing easy. But is it safe/desirable? 52	 What are high-wage occupations in the Express Entry system 
53	 How we determine eligible high-wage occupations for Express Entry 
54	 Express Entry high-wage occupations list 
55	 What are high-wage occupations in the Express Entry system? 
56	 Under Express Entry, a job is considered a high-wage occupation if the median wage of all people in Canada performing that job is at least 1.3 times higher than the average median wage of the overall Canadian work force. 
57	 This is based on all the people in Canada working under the same National Occupational Classification (NOC). 
58	 It is not determined based on a person’s specific job position or salary. 
59	 High-wage occupations are grouped into 3 levels using NOC codes where the median wage is at least: 
60	 twice the average median wage
61	 1.5 times, but less than twice, the average median wage 
62	 1.3 times, but less than 1.5 times, the average median wage 
63	 How we determine eligible high-wage occupations for Express Entry
64	 We use data from these sources over the last 3 years to determine the high-wage occupation level for each job:
65	 The Job Bank 
66	 The Labour Force Survey , and 
67	 The Census of Population . 
68	 For each NOC, its high-wage occupation level is determined based on the highest level its median wage met in the last 3 years.
69	 What happens to my application if the high-wage occupation list is updated?
70	 If the high-wage occupation list changes after we issue an Invitation to Apply (ITA), we’ll keep using the level that applied on the date we invited you. 
71	 This applies if a job:
72	 moves levels on the list 
73	 is removed from the list, or 
74	 is added to the list
75	 Express Entry high-wage occupations list 
76	 Comes into effect on November 3, 2026
77	 The list is currently based on data from 2023 to 2025.

introduce points for eligible Canadian work experience or qualifying job offers in high-­wage occupations , and
 remove labour market impact assessment (LMIA) requirements for qualifying job offers used to establish program eligibility and obtain Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) points
 What candidates need to know
 Candidates who may qualify for job offer points should review and update their Express Entry profiles before November 3 to verify that all required job offer information is included and accurate.
 How the new points will work
 Candidates may qualify for points based on either
 eligible Canadian work experience based on its duration, with additional points where the experience is in a high-wage occupation, or
 a qualifying job offer in a high-wage occupation
 Candidates who qualify under both will receive whichever option provides more points. The points for Canadian work experience and a job offer will not be combined.
 The maximum number of points available under the labour market integration factor is 150 points for candidates without an accompanying spouse or common-law partner and 140 points for candidates with an accompanying spouse or common-law partner.
 Receiving additional CRS points does not guarantee an invitation to apply. Invitations will continue to depend on the requirements and CRS cut-off score for each invitation round.
 Points for Canadian work experience in a high-wage occupation
 Candidates with at least one year of eligible Canadian work experience in a high-wage occupation may receive additional CRS points based on the wage level of their occupation.
 High-wage occupation level | 
 Additional CRS points | 
 At least 12 months in one or more occupations at 2 times the median | 
 70 | 
 If not eligible for 70 points, at least 12 months combined in occupations at 1.5 times the median or above | 
 40 | 
 If not eligible for 40 or 70 points, at least 12 months combined across eligible high-wage occupations (1.3 times the median or above) | 
 20 | 
 These points are in addition to a candidate's CRS score based on the duration of their eligible Canadian work experience, up to a maximum of 80 points for 5 years. Combined, candidates with eligible Canadian work experience in a high-wage occupation could receive up to 150 points for Canadian work experience.
 Candidates with Canadian work experience that does not qualify for high-wage occupation points will continue to receive points for the duration of their eligible Canadian work experience.
 Eligible Canadian work experience generally must have been acquired in Canada within the previous 10 years in an occupation in TEER category 0, 1, 2 or 3 of the National Occupational Classification. Specific provisions also apply to certain physicians providing publicly funded medical services.
 Points for a qualifying job offer in a high-wage occupation
 Candidates with a qualifying job offer in a high-wage occupation may receive: 
 High-wage occupation level | 
 CRS points | 
 At least 2 times the median wage | 
 100 | 
 At least 1.5 times the median wage | 
 70 | 
 At least 1.3 times the median wage | 
 50 | 
 A qualifying job offer must generally be for full-time, continuous work in Canada for at least one year after the candidate becomes a permanent resident.
 Specific requirements apply to certain occupations, including skilled trades and physicians providing publicly funded medical services.
 Single assessment process for qualifying job offers
 Beginning November 3, 2026, an LMIA will not be required for a qualifying job offer to be eligible for the new Express Entry points. 
 A temporary public policy will also exempt candidates invited to apply on or after November 3, 2026, from all requirements related to LMIA and LMIA exemptions for qualifying job offers used to establish eligibility under the Federal Skilled Worker Program and Federal Skilled Trades Program , provided they meet the conditions of the public policy.
 IRCC will continue to verify qualifying job offers and take measures to identify and address potential fraud or misrepresentation. Limiting job offer points to high-wage occupations also supports verification, as many of these occupations require specialized skills, experience or qualifications that can be assessed as part of the application.
 How job offers will be assessed
 An IRCC officer must determine that a qualifying job offer is genuine, including whether
 the employer is actively engaged in the business for which the offer is being made
 the offer reflects the employer's reasonable employment needs
 the employer can reasonably meet the terms of the offer
 the candidate is qualified and able to perform the work and is likely to accept and carry out the employment
 the employer has complied with applicable federal and provincial employment and recruitment laws
 A job offer that is revoked will no longer qualify.

25 : 13;\n  return languageExcellent ? 50 : 25;\n}\n\nfunction educationWorkPoints(\n  education: CrsInputs[\"education\"],\n  canadianYears: number,\n) {\n  const tier = educationTransferTier(education);\n  if (tier === \"secondary\" || canadianYears < 1) return 0;\n\n  if (tier === \"oneYear\") return canadianYears >= 2 ? 25 : 13;\n  return canadianYears >= 2 ? 50 : 25;\n}\n\nfunction foreignLanguagePoints(\n  foreignWork: CrsInputs[\"foreignWorkYears\"],\n  languageGood: boolean,\n  languageExcellent: boolean,\n) {\n  if (foreignWork === \"none\" || !languageGood) return 0;\n\n  if (foreignWork === \"oneToTwo\") return languageExcellent ? 25 : 13;\n  return languageExcellent ? 50 : 25;\n}\n\nfunction foreignWorkPoints(\n  foreignWork: CrsInputs[\"foreignWorkYears\"],\n  canadianYears: number,\n) {\n  if (foreignWork === \"none\" || canadianYears < 1) return 0;\n\n  if (foreignWork === \"oneToTwo\") return canadianYears >= 2 ? 25 : 13;\n  return canadianYears >= 2 ? 50 : 25;\n}\n\nfunction certificatePoints(\n  hasCertificate: boolean,\n  languageGood: boolean,\n  languageAtLeastFive: boolean,\n) {\n  if (!hasCertificate) return 0;\n  if (languageGood) return 50;\n  if (languageAtLeastFive) return 25;\n  return 0;\n}\n\nexport function calculateCrs(inputs: CrsInputs): CrsResult {\n  const hasSpouse = inputs.maritalStatus === \"withSpouse\";\n  const spouseIndex = hasSpouse ? 0 : 1;\n\n  const age = Math.min(45, Math.max(17, Math.round(inputs.age)));\n  const agePoints = AGE_POINTS[age]?.[spouseIndex] ?? 0;\n  const educationPoints = CORE_EDUCATION_POINTS[inputs.education][spouseIndex];\n  const firstLanguagePoints = ABILITIES.reduce(\n    (sum, ability) =>\n      sum + FIRST_LANGUAGE_POINTS[inputs.firstLanguage[ability]][spouseIndex],\n    0,\n  );\n  const secondLanguagePoints = inputs.hasSecondLanguage\n    ? Math.min(\n        ABILITIES.reduce(\n          (sum, ability) =>\n            sum + SECOND_LANGUAGE_POINTS[inputs.secondLanguage[ability]],\n          0,\n        ),\n        hasSpouse ? 22 : 24,\n      )\n    : 0;\n  const canadianWorkYearsValue = WORK_YEARS_VALUE[inputs.canadianWorkYears];\n  const canadianWorkPoints =\n    CANADIAN_WORK_POINTS[inputs.canadianWorkYears][spouseIndex];\n\n  const corePoints =\n    agePoints +\n    educationPoints +\n    firstLanguagePoints +\n    secondLanguagePoints +\n    canadianWorkPoints;\n\n  const coreItems: BreakdownItem[] = [\n    { label: \"Age\", points: agePoints },\n    { label: \"Level of education\", points: educationPoints },\n    { label: \"First official language\", points: firstLanguagePoints },\n  ];\n  if (secondLanguagePoints > 0) {\n    coreItems.push({\n      label: \"Second official language\",\n      points: secondLanguagePoints,\n    });\n  }\n  coreItems.push({ label: \"Canadian work experience\", points: canadianWorkPoints });\n\n  const spouseEducationPoints = hasSpouse\n    ? SPOUSE_EDUCATION_POINTS[inputs.spouseEducation ?? \"lessThanSecondary\"]\n    : 0;\n  const spouseLanguagePoints = hasSpouse\n    ? Math.min(\n        20,\n        ABILITIES.reduce(\n          (sum, ability) =>\n            sum +\n            SPOUSE_LANGUAGE_POINTS[\n              inputs.spouseFirstLanguage?.[ability] ?? \"below5\"\n            ],\n          0,\n        ),\n      )\n    : 0;\n  const spouseWorkPoints = hasSpouse\n    ? SPOUSE_WORK_POINTS[inputs.spouseCanadianWorkYears ?? \"none\"]\n    : 0;\n  const spousePoints =\n    spouseEducationPoints + spouseLanguagePoints + spouseWorkPoints;\n\n  const languageGood = allFirstLanguageAtLeast(inputs.firstLanguage, 7);\n  const languageExcellent = allFirstLanguageAtLeast(inputs.firstLanguage, 9);\n  const languageAtLeastFive = allFirstLanguageAtLeast(inputs.firstLanguage, 5);\n\n  const transferItems: BreakdownItem[] = [\n    {\n      label: \"Education + language\",\n      points: educationLanguagePoints(\n        inputs.education,\n        languageGood,\n        languageExcellent,\n      ),\n    },\n    {\n      label: \"Education + Canadian work\",\n      points: educationWorkPoints(inputs.education, canadianWorkYearsValue),\n    },\n    {\n      label: \"Foreign work + language\",\n      points: foreignLanguagePoints(\n        inputs.foreignWorkYears,\n        languageGood,\n        languageExcellent,\n      ),\n    },\n    {\n      label: \"Foreign work + Canadian work\",\n      points: foreignWorkPoints(\n        inputs.foreignWorkYears,\n        canadianWorkYearsValue,\n      ),\n    },\n    {\n      label: \"Certificate of qualification + language\",\n      points: certificatePoints(\n        inputs.certificateOfQualification,\n        languageGood,\n        languageAtLeastFive,\n      ),\n    },\n  ].filter((item) => item.points > 0);\n\n  const transferabilityPoints = Math.min(\n    100,\n    transferItems.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.points, 0),\n  );\n\n  const additionalItems: BreakdownItem[] = [];\n  if (inputs.siblingInCanada) {\n    additionalItems.push({ label: \"Brother or sister in Canada\", points: 15 });\n  }\n  if (inputs.frenchNclb7) {\n    additionalItems.push({\n      label: \"French language skills\",\n      points: languageAtLeastFive ? 50 : 25,\n    });\n  }\n  if (inputs.canadianEducation === \"oneOrTwoYears\") {\n    additionalItems.push({\n      label: \"Post-secondary education in Canada\",\n      points: 15,\n    });\n  } else if (inputs.canadianEducation === \"threePlusYears\") {\n    additionalItems.push({\n      label: \"Post-secondary education in Canada\",\n      points: 30,\n    });\n  }\n  if (inputs.provincialNomination) {\n    additionalItems.push({\n      label: \"Provincial or territorial nomination\",\n      points: 600,\n    });\n  }\n  const additionalPoints = additionalItems.reduce(\n    (sum, item) => sum + item.points,\n    0,\n  );\n\n  const total = corePoints + spousePoints + transferabilityPoints + additionalPoints;\n\n  return {\n    total,\n    band: scoreBand(total),\n    core: corePoints,\n    spouse: spousePoints,\n    transferability: transferabilityPoints,\n    additional: additionalPoints,\n    sections: [\n      {\n        key: \"core\",\n        label: \"Core human capital\",\n        points: corePoints,\n        max: hasSpouse ? 460 : 500,\n        items: coreItems,\n      },\n      ...(hasSpouse\n        ? [\n            {\n              key: \"spouse\" as const,\n              label: \"Spouse or partner\",\n              points: spousePoints,\n              max: 40,\n              items: [\n                { label: \"Education\", points: spouseEducationPoints },\n                { label: \"Official language\", points: spouseLanguagePoints },\n                { label: \"Canadian work experience\", points: spouseWorkPoints },\n              ],\n            },\n          ]\n        : []),\n      {\n        key: \"transferability\",\n        label: \"Skill transferability\",\n        points: transferabilityPoints,\n        max: 100,\n        items: transferItems,\n      },\n      {\n        key: \"additional\",\n        label: \"Additional points\",\n        points: additionalPoints,\n        max: 600,\n        items: additionalItems,\n      },\n    ],\n    rulesVersion: CRS_RULES.version,\n    rulesEffectiveFrom: CRS_RULES.effectiveFrom,\n    rulesLastVerified: CRS_RULES.lastVerified,\n    rulesSourceUrl: CRS_RULES.sourceUrl,\n    nextChangeDate: CRS_RULES.nextChangeDate,\n    nextChangeNote: CRS_RULES.nextChangeNote,\n    benchmark: BENCHMARK,\n  };\n}\n"

(JSON.parse(raw) as T) : null;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nexport function writeLocalValue(key: string, value: unknown) {\n  const store = storage();\n  if (!store) return;\n  try {\n    store.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(value));\n  } catch {\n    // Storage can be full or blocked; the score still shows for this session.\n  }\n}\n\nexport function removeLocalValue(key: string) {\n  const store = storage();\n  if (!store) return;\n  try {\n    store.removeItem(key);\n  } catch {\n    // Ignore unavailable storage.\n  }\n}\n"

`mapleroute.crs.user.${userId}`\n    : \"mapleroute.crs.preview\";\n}\n\nexport function CrsProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  const { user, previewMode } = useAuth();\n  const [latest, setLatest] = useState<SavedScore | null>(null);\n  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    let active = true;\n    const userId = user?.id ?? null;\n\n    if (!userId && !previewMode) {\n      setLatest(null);\n      setLoading(false);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const fallback = readLocalValue<SavedScore>(cacheKey(userId));\n\n    async function load() {\n      setLoading(true);\n\n      if (userId && supabase) {\n        const { data, error } = await supabase\n          .from(\"crs_snapshots\")\n          .select(\"score, breakdown, inputs, created_at\")\n          .eq(\"user_id\", userId)\n          .order(\"created_at\", { ascending: false })\n          .limit(1)\n          .maybeSingle();\n\n        if (!active) return;\n\n        if (!error && data) {\n          const row = data as {\n            score: number;\n            breakdown: CrsResult;\n            inputs: CrsInputs;\n            created_at: string;\n          };\n          setLatest({\n            score: row.score,\n            band: row.breakdown?.band ?? fallback?.band ?? \"low\",\n            result: row.breakdown,\n            inputs: row.inputs,\n            createdAt: row.created_at,\n            source: \"account\",\n          });\n          setLoading(false);\n          return;\n        }\n      }\n\n      if (!active) return;\n      setLatest(fallback);\n      setLoading(false);\n    }\n\n    void load();\n\n    return () => {\n      active = false;\n    };\n  }, [user?.id, previewMode]);\n\n  const save = useCallback(\n    async (result: CrsResult, inputs: CrsInputs) => {\n      const userId = user?.id ?? null;\n      const entry: SavedScore = {\n        score: result.total,\n        band: result.band,\n        result,\n        inputs,\n        createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),\n        source: userId ? \"account\" : \"device\",\n      };\n\n      writeLocalValue(cacheKey(userId), entry);\n      setLatest(entry);\n\n      if (!userId || !supabase) {\n        return { synced: false };\n      }\n\n      const { error } = await supabase.from(\"crs_snapshots\").insert({\n        user_id: userId,\n        score: result.total,\n        breakdown: result,\n        inputs,\n        rules_version: result.rulesVersion,\n      });\n\n      if (!error) {\n        const syncedEntry: SavedScore = { ...entry, source: \"account\" };\n        writeLocalValue(cacheKey(userId), syncedEntry);\n        setLatest(syncedEntry);\n        return { synced: true };\n      }\n\n      return { synced: false };\n    },\n    [user?.id],\n  );\n\n  const value = useMemo(\n    () => ({ latest, loading, save }),\n    [latest, loading, save],\n  );\n\n  return <CrsContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</CrsContext.Provider>;\n}\n\nexport function useCrs() {\n  const value = useContext(CrsContext);\n  if (!value) {\n    throw new Error(\"useCrs must be used inside CrsProvider\");\n  }\n  return value;\n}\n"
}
